title: phase_0
text: For equally likely outcomes, probability is favorable outcomes divided by all outcomes. The equally likely condition matters. A fair die has six equally likely faces, so three even faces give probability one half.

title: phase_1
text: For successive events, multiply the first probability by the conditional probability of the second. In a bag with three red and two blue balls, drawing two reds without replacement has probability three fifths times two fourths.

title: phase_2
text: At least one red includes exactly one red and two reds. It is often easier to exclude the opposite event: no red. Two blues have probability two fifths times one fourth. Subtract this from one.

title: phase_3
text: Add probabilities for disjoint alternatives. If alternatives overlap, subtract the overlap once. Multiplication and addition are chosen from the event structure, not from keywords alone. Name the event before calculating.
